message: Thanks, I'll help you check. With $423,800 in household work income, most of these programs are likely out of reach. The main one still worth checking is the child tax credit, which depends on children and whether you're married. How many children under 18 live with you, and is there a married couple in the household?
reply: I have my son. Yes, my husband and I.

summary: Household: two married adults in their thirties, one child under 18, all healthy, household work income $423,800 a year. None of the ten programmes appear to be available at this income level. SNAP, WIC, TANF, SSI, Medicaid, CHIP, school meals and EITC all have income limits far below this. The ACA premium tax credit phases out well below this income. The refundable part of the child tax credit is about $0 because the credit is fully phased out at this income and the household's tax liability would absorb any nonrefundable portion. Screening based on the income and household details given; no state-specific rules were checked, since no state program would reach this income.
